summary: Save the command as a playbook that sets hosts, connection and modules, plus a debug task to display results (module output isn't printed by default); run it with ansible-playbook -i host, -u -k -e.
questions: How do I turn an ad hoc network command into a playbook?
Why doesn't my playbook print the module output?

answer_card.title: First network playbook
answer_card.answer_md:
The playbook sets `hosts: all`, `connection: ansible.netcommon.network_cli` and the module per task, so you can drop them from the command line. Module output stays in memory for later tasks rather than printing, so add a `debug` task to see it.
```bash
ansible-playbook -i vyos.example.net, -u ansible -k -e ansible_network_os=vyos.vyos.vyos first_playbook.yml
```
